chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who marries off his daughter: Is it permissible for him to eat from her dowry? He said, 'He is not permitted to do so.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ: he is not permitted to do so

ai.seo_question: Can a father keep the dowry of his daughter when he marries her off?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the father's right to the dowry (mahr) is clarified as belonging exclusively to the daughter, distinguishing it from the father's potential right to maintenance (nafaqah) during the marriage. This ruling underscores the daughter's financial autonomy in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the bride receives her due compensation directly rather than it being absorbed by the father who arranged the union.
